chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

A man said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Have you left Jihad and its hardship, and adhered to Hajj and its ease?' He said: 'And he (peace be upon him) was reclining, so he sat up and said: 'Woe to you! Has it not reached you what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said during the Farewell Pilgrimage? Indeed, when he stood at Arafat and the sun inclined to set, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Bilal! Say to the people, so let them be silent.' So when they were silent, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Your Lord has extended favor upon you in this day, so He forgave your good-doers, and your good-doers interceded for your evil-doers. Therefore depart, forgiven for you.'
He said: 'And others than al-Thumali added that he said: 'Except for the people of liabilities (debts/obligations), for Allah is Just. He takes for the weak from the strong.'

So when it was the night of Jam' (Arafat), he did not cease to converse with his Lord and ask Him for the people of liabilities. So when he stood at Jam', he said to Bilal: 'Say to the people, so let them be silent!' So when they were silent, he said: 'Your Lord has extended favor upon you in this day, so He forgave your good-doers, and your good-doers interceded for your evil-doers. Therefore depart, forgiven for you, and He guaranteed for the people of liabilities from His presence the satisfaction (of their creditors).'

key_terms.أَهْلَ التَّبِعَاتِ: People of liabilities (those with debts/obligations to others)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'liabilities' (tabi'at) in the Prophet's Farewell Sermon at Arafat?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) refutes the notion that Hajj is inferior to Jihad by highlighting the unique spiritual efficacy of the Day of Arafat, where divine mercy is amplified through intercession. He specifically addresses the 'Ahl al-Taba'at' (those with financial or social obligations to others), whose sins are often hindered by unpaid debts, by narrating that God guarantees their satisfaction (Rida) from the Divine treasury. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on social justice and the purification of the soul through settling rights (Huquq al-Ibad) as a prerequisite for complete spiritual acceptance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said,

‘A man said to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> neglected the Jihad and necessitated the Hajj and its softness?’ He said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> was reclining, so he<sup>asws</sup> sat up and said: ‘Woe be unto you! Has it not reached you what Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said in the Farewell Hajj? It was when he<sup>saww</sup> had paused at Arafat and the sun had inclined to set, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Bilal! Say to the people, so let them be silent’. So when they were silent, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Your Lord<sup>azwj</sup> has Extended (Favours) upon you in this day, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Forgave your good-doers, and Interceded for your good-doers regarding your evil-doers. Therefore depart (with your sins having been) Forgiven for you’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And (narrators) other than Al-Sumaly have increased that, ‘He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Except for the people with the liabilities, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Just. He<sup>azwj</sup> Takes for the weak ones, from the strong ones’.

So when it was the night of Friday, he<sup>saww</sup> did not cease to whisper to his<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> asked Him<sup>azwj</sup> for the people with the liabilities. So when he<sup>saww</sup> paused at Jam’a, said to Bilal: ‘Say to the people, so let them be silent!’ So when they were silent, he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Your Lord<sup>azwj</sup> has Extended (Favours) upon you in this day, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Forgave your good-doers, and Interceded for your good-doers regarding your evil-doers. Therefore depart (with your sins having been) Forgiven for you, and He<sup>azwj</sup> has Taken the Responsibility for the people with the liabilities of the pleasure (of their creditors) from His<sup>azwj</sup> Presence’.
en.sarwar: 24. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from abu Hamzah al-Thumafiy who has said the following:

“A man once said to Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘You have given up Jihad because it is harsh, but you have attached yourself to Hajj because it is comfortable.’ He (the Imam) who was leaning sat up straight and said, ‘Fie upon you. Have you not heard what the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said during his farewell pilgrimage during his stay in ‘Arafat, and it was about sunset. The Messenger of Allah said, ‘O Bilal, ask people to remain silent.’ When people became silent the Messenger of Allah said, ‘Your Lord has granted you favors on this day. He has granted forgiveness to the individuals of good deeds, and has made the ones of good deed to intercede for the ones of evil deeds. You can leave now with your sins forgiven.’

Narrators other than abu Hamzah al-Thumaliy have mentioned that the Imam additionally said, ‘Except those who are of individuals of al-Tabi‘at (acts that require investigation).’ Allah is just. He brings to justice the stronger ones who wrong the weaker ones.

On the night of al-Jam‘ he continued quietly speaking to his Lord and asked Him for forgiveness for the individuals of al-Tabi‘at. When he stayed in Jam‘ he said to Bilal. ‘You should ask people to remain silent.’ When people became silent he (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Your Lord has granted you favors on this day. He has forgiven the individuals of good deeds among you. He has made the individuals of good deeds among you to intercede on behalf of the individuals of evil deeds. You now may leave with your sins forgiven and He has made an undertaking in favor of the individuals of al- Tabi‘at (people liable for the rights of others) to be happy with them.’”
